steps.label: open the Tiles tab
steps.goal: tile authoring lives there, and the key list changes with the tab. The tab opens a blank tile for you, already named after the kit
do: press 3
steps.recovery: if a text field has the keyboard the number types into it: press Escape first

steps.label: bring a floor in
steps.goal: a tile with nothing in it has no size and no edges, so the floor comes first. It fills the tile, so the arrows have nowhere to take it -- movement starts with the wall
do: walk the library with up and down -- Shift strides five
press Enter on site/floor
steps.checkpoint: the tile has a piece in it
steps.recovery: if the list is empty a filter is hiding it: press Backspace until the filter clears

steps.label: the piece should be in hand
steps.goal: Enter both drops the piece and hands it to the arrows, no Space needed -- and the held piece is slightly brighter than a set one, resolving to its true colours when you press Escape
do: nothing to press
look: the held piece carries a subtle brightness lift
steps.recovery: press Escape and then Enter again; if the arrows still walk the list, that is the bug back

steps.label: bring a wall in as well
steps.goal: two pieces is where a tile stops being a mesh with extra steps -- and the arrows will not walk the library while a piece is in hand
do: press Escape to put the floor down
walk to site/wall -- the plain wall
press Enter
steps.recovery: if the arrows move the piece instead of the list, Escape did not land: the panel says which of the two states the tab is in

steps.label: walk the wall with the arrows and J
steps.goal: new: the arrows walk stops on the wall's own span, so centre and flush are always reachable. At the top of the ladder one press from centre lands flush; J divides the span in thirds, then ninths, then wraps back
do: press each of the four arrows and watch where it lands
press Q or E to turn the view, then an arrow again
press J and nudge, then J again, then once more to wrap
steps.recovery: if the arrows walk the list instead, the piece is not in hand: press Space to take it

steps.label: put the wall against one side
steps.goal: Shift+arrow is still the flush verb, and it lands on the same outermost stop the plain arrows end at -- one coordinate system, not two
do: hold Shift and press an arrow
the wall goes hard against that side
steps.recovery: if the panel says nothing moved, the piece already fills that axis and it names the axis that would

steps.label: walk it back to the centre
steps.goal: the return trip that used to be impossible: flush is a stop on the ladder now, so plain presses walk it back and the centre is exactly one ladder away
do: press the plain arrow that points back toward the middle
at the top of the ladder one press lands dead centre
press J first to come back in thirds instead
steps.recovery: if it overshoots or lands beside a drawn line, say so -- the drawn stops ARE the reachable positions, and a mismatch is the finding

steps.label: is the tile still one cell
steps.goal: only a one-cell tile can be a solver prototype, and the size is read off the contents: a piece off centre costs DOUBLE its offset, because the tile is centred on its anchor and has to reach that far both ways
do: read the size line at the top of the panel
if it is bigger than 1 x 1, the line under it names the piece
steps.recovery: focus that piece with , and . then walk it back toward the middle with the plain arrows

steps.label: save it
steps.goal: so the kit gains it and the Map palette can place it
do: press Cmd+S
steps.recovery: an empty tile is refused by name; so is an id the vocabulary does not accept

steps.label: reopen tile_4 from the kit
steps.goal: the kit is a tab on the list and reopening lands you editing -- and tile_4 ships wrong: its low wall sits dead centre, so all four edges derive open and the solver treats it as a second floor tile
do: press Escape to put the piece down
press right to show the KIT tab
walk down to site/tile_4
press right again to open it
steps.recovery: Escape backs out of the kit list; if right does nothing, you are still holding a piece

steps.label: flush the low wall against a side
steps.goal: this is the real repair: once the wall touches the boundary, that face derives closed and tile_4 stops reading as a second floor tile
do: press , or . until the low wall is the focused piece
hold Shift and press an arrow -- or use the plain arrow, flush is the last stop
steps.recovery: if nothing moved, it is already flush on that axis: pick another side

steps.label: save the repair
steps.goal: Cmd+S writes over the committed tile_4, and the kit leaves this exercise one tile better than it shipped
do: press Cmd+S
steps.recovery: if the save is refused the panel names why -- the id is already good, so it will be the members

steps.label: does it read as a tile
steps.goal: the last question no checkpoint can answer, and the reason this exercise has a person in it
do: look at tile_4 in the 3d view
then say what you want changed about tile creation -- keys, panels, flow, anything
steps.recovery: there is nothing to recover here: an answer of no is the finding
